a.text: A revolving three-year plan (1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028) with one initiative: sensor-based corrosion-inhibitor dosing on ageing onshore flowlines.

b.text: Purpose: reduce corrosion-related leaks and unplanned shutdowns on ageing flowlines. Expected outcome: Cut leak incidents on the three pilot flowlines by at least 25% and unplanned shutdown hours by at least 20% within 12 months of full dosing control, against the 2025 baseline.

c.text: One initiative. Objectives: (1) install sensors on three flowlines; (2) build a dosing model from field data; (3) test automated dosing; (4) compare incident and shutdown records with the 2025 baseline.

d.text: Research scope: advanced (applied). Field data modelling and controlled dosing trials.

e.text: Planned expenditure over the plan period is ₦30.0 million, shown by year in the table below.

f.text: Corrosion-rate monitoring to NACE/AMPP-aligned practice and laboratory inhibitor tests to ASTM G31 immersion-test procedure; dosing model validated on held-out field data. Equipment: corrosion probes, flow and pressure sensors, a dosing controller. The procedures align with internationally accepted standards.

g.text: Three onshore flowlines at Sample Field-3, Bayelsa State; laboratory tests at the research centre, Port Harcourt.

h.text: Estimated duration of the research: 36 months (1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028).

i.text: Sponsoring institution: Sample Institute of Materials and Corrosion Research, Port Harcourt (fictional). Director: Prof. Emeka Dike-Sample. Officer in charge: Dr. Halima Sani-Sample.

j.text: Reduced leaks lower the risk of spills. Inhibitor use is dosed to need, and discharge is monitored under the Company's environmental management plan. Laboratory waste follows the institute's protocol.

k.text: The Company proposes a Board representative on the steering team and invites the Board to attend the pilot review.

l.text: The Company will call for research-partner proposals for scale-up to further flowlines after the pilot, in 2028.

m.text: The Pipeline Integrity Manager (Engr. Femi Lawal-Sample) leads implementation, with the Corrosion Engineer and Local Content Officer as key officers.

n.text: Methodology and requirements: sensor installation, data collection, model building, dosing trials and baseline comparison. Requirements: three flowlines, a dosing controller and a data analyst.

o.text: Six Company technicians trained in sensor maintenance and dosing control; one MSc student attached; one industrial attachment each year.

p.text: Phase 1 (2026): installation and baseline. Phase 2 (2027): model building and dosing trials. Phase 3 (2028): comparison and final report. Milestones are in Annex 1, section 6.

expected_outcome_text: Cut leak incidents on the three pilot flowlines by at least 25% and unplanned shutdown hours by at least 20% within 12 months of full dosing control, against the 2025 baseline.

board_notices.description: Board notice of a deviation in the sensor-installation schedule; corrected schedule filed on the fourteenth day.

project.title: Optimising Corrosion-Inhibitor Dosing in Ageing Onshore Oil Flowlines Using Field Sensor Data to Reduce Leak Incidents and Unplanned Production Shutdowns
project.goals_and_objectives: Install sensors on three flowlines; build a dosing model from field data; test automated dosing; measure leak incidents and shutdown hours against the 2025 baseline. The project addresses avoidable leaks and lost production on ageing assets.
